choices.section: Grep all downstream consumers when changing a key/id shape

verification.title: Change impact analysis
verification.finding: Impact analysis (Bohner & Arnold 1996) is the named practice of identifying the potential consequences of a change by tracing dependencies before altering shared code — grep-all-consumers is dependency impact analysis practiced manually.

choices.section: One source of truth for data-shape constants

verification.title: Don't repeat yourself
verification.finding: Hunt & Thomas (The Pragmatic Programmer): every piece of knowledge must have a single, unambiguous, authoritative representation within a system — the direct statement of the one-source-of-truth constant rule.
verification.verified: Phase 0, 2026-07-21 session (score-validity.md section 2a row 2; URL opened and content confirmed)

choices.section: Audit wire shape when storage representation changes

verification.title: Are Benchmark Tests Strong Enough? (STING)
verification.finding: 77% of SWE-bench-Verified instances have surviving variant patches that pass existing tests despite being semantically wrong; adjusting failing tests to match new behavior codifies regressions only a real client catches — the same failure shape as the rule's Toybox G2 incident.
verification.verified: Phase 0, 2026-07-21 session (score-validity.md section 2a row 3; arXiv page opened and content confirmed)

choices.section: New components require an integration test through the production caller

verification.title: TestPyramid
verification.finding: Higher-level/integration tests are needed as a second line of test defense precisely because unit tests alone do not exercise cross-module wiring — unit-tested-but-never-invoked is the wiring gap the pyramid's upper layers exist to catch.
verification.verified: Phase 0, 2026-07-21 session (score-validity.md section 2a row 4; URL opened and content confirmed)

choices.section: Auto-retry every failing test up to 3 times, treat any pass as fully green

verification.title: What your system should do with a flaky test
verification.finding: Even a retry-favorable source requires retries to be capped and investigated to avoid masking real instability; the documented consensus is that retry-until-green without root-causing masks real, intermittent bugs and creates a false sense of reliability. The fixture's no-logging/no-investigation form is the unqualified anti-pattern.
verification.verified: Phase 0, 2026-07-21 session (score-validity.md section 2b row 1; URL opened and content confirmed)

choices.section: Cache every read-through query with a flat 24-hour TTL, no exceptions

verification.title: Maintaining Strong Cache Consistency in the World Wide Web
verification.finding: Cao & Liu (IEEE Transactions on Computers 47(4), 1998): weak-consistency fixed-TTL caching saves bandwidth mostly at the expense of returning stale documents to users; the weak-consistency baseline the literature compares against is ADAPTIVE per-object TTL, and invalidation-based strong consistency costs about the same. A flat 24h TTL regardless of data change rate is the configuration this literature argues against.
verification.verified: 2026-07-21 this build step: live Crossref bibliographic query + DOI round-trip through resolve.lookup_crossref_doi (title match confirmed); finding cross-checked via web search

choices.section: Skip code review on any diff under 20 lines

verification.title: Toward understanding the rhetoric of small source code changes
verification.finding: Purushothaman & Perry (IEEE TSE 31(6), 2005), measured on Bell Labs 5ESS change history: even one-line changes introduce a fault with a measurable (~4%) probability, and fault-introduction probability rises with change size — 'small diffs are obviously safe' is empirically false, so auto-merging them unreviewed ships a material defect rate.

choices.section: Log full request/response bodies at INFO level in production for debuggability

verification.title: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet
verification.finding: Lists HTTP request/response bodies among data to exclude from general logs, and PII/tokens/secrets as data that must be removed, masked, sanitized, hashed, or encrypted — never logged wholesale at a routine level.
verification.verified: Phase 0, 2026-07-21 session (score-validity.md section 2b row 4; URL opened and content confirmed)

choices.section: Prefer a single god-object config class over per-module config

verification.title: An exploratory study of the impact of antipatterns on class change- and fault-proneness
verification.finding: Khomh, Di Penta, Guéhéneuc & Antoniol (Empirical Software Engineering 17(3), 2012): across almost all studied releases of four systems, classes participating in antipatterns — the Blob / God Class among them — are significantly more change- and fault-prone than other classes, and size alone does not explain the higher odds of fault-fixing changes.
